title: Four Color Theorem: Survey for Lean 4 Formalization
description: Survey of re-formalizing Gonthier's Coq proof of the Four Color Theorem in Lean 4. Proves small cases (≤4 vertices, bipartite), assesses feasibility (~43K lines needed), and identifies starting points.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Survey file with basic colorability results from Mathlib.

overview.problemStatement: Can the Four Color Theorem (Gonthier 2005 Coq proof) be re-formalized in Lean 4?
overview.text: Survey: 4CT formalization requires ~43K lines. Proves small cases. Identifies starting points.
keyInsights: Gonthier's Coq proof was ~60K lines; Lean 4 estimate ~43K with native_decide
Planar graph formalization is the key missing infrastructure in Mathlib
Five Color Theorem (~2000 lines) is a feasible intermediate target
native_decide could replace much of the computational kernel
overview.proofStrategy: Survey: 4CT formalization requires ~43K lines. Proves small cases. Identifies starting points.

conclusion.summary: A full 4CT in Lean 4 is a multi-year project. The recommended path: planar graphs → Five Color Theorem → reducibility framework → computational verification via native_decide.
conclusion.implications: A full 4CT in Lean 4 is a multi-year project. The recommended path: planar graphs → Five Color Theorem → reducibility framework → computational verification via native_decide.

crossReferences.description: Addresses 4CT question from Euler formula context
